import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from src.exporter import export_rows
from src.csv_exporter import export_csv
from src.json_exporter import export_json

# CSV header even with no rows; LF endings; standard quoting.
assert export_rows([], "csv") == "id,name\n"
assert export_rows([{"id": "a,b", "name": 'say "hi"\nnow'}], "csv") == 'id,name\n"a,b","say ""hi""\nnow"\n'

# JSON options and stringification.
assert export_rows([{"id": 1, "name": "Alice"}], "json") == '[{"id":"1","name":"Alice"}]'
assert export_rows([], "json") == "[]"
assert export_rows([{"id": "é", "name": None}], "json") == '[{"id":"é","name":""}]'

# Only id and name are kept; missing keys become ''.
assert export_rows([{"id": 2, "extra": "x"}], "json") == '[{"id":"2","name":""}]'

# Unsupported format.
try:
    export_rows([], "xml")
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")

# One-shot iterables are supported and not mutated.
rows = ({"id": i, "name": f"n{i}"} for i in range(3))
assert export_rows(rows, "csv") == "id,name\n0,n0\n1,n1\n2,n2\n"

source = [{"id": 1, "name": "Alice"}]
snapshot = [dict(r) for r in source]
export_rows(source, "json")
export_rows(source, "csv")
assert source == snapshot, "input must not be mutated"

# Wrappers delegate to the shared entry point and agree with it.
data = [{"id": 1, "name": "Alice"}, {"id": 2}, {"id": "x,y", "name": None}]
assert export_csv(data) == export_rows(data, "csv")
assert export_json(data) == export_rows(data, "json")

print("exporter checks passed")
